draft.title: Responsible consumption
card: Responsible consumption means people think about the effects of what they buy and use. They try to cut those effects.
buy and use less. Reuse: use an item again, or for a new job, instead of throwing it away.
fix a broken item so it lasts longer. Recycle: break down used materials, such as paper or glass, so they can be made into new products.
People can also choose products made sustainably. This means buying goods made in ways that cause less harm to the environment and treat workers fairly.
draft.remember: Buy less, use things longer, recycle what is left, and choose products made sustainably.

a.q: Sam's school bag zip breaks. He takes it to a shop to have the zip fixed instead of buying a new bag. Which action is this?
a.why: Sam fixes the broken item so it lasts longer, which is repairing. It is not recycling, because the bag is not broken down into materials to make new products.
a.clue: Was the bag fixed, or broken down?

b.q: Priya's family in Orange needs a new jacket. They choose one made from recycled materials by a company that pays its workers fairly. Which idea does this best show?
opts: Repairing an item they already own
Reusing an item for a new job
b.why: The family picked a product made in a sustainable way, using recycled materials and fair pay. They still bought a new jacket, so they did not reduce what they buy. They did not fix or reuse an old item either.
b.clue: Look at how the jacket was made, not just that it was bought.
